source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #352 (branch fix/334-borrowed-drop at head 8ad5fb42bf4e164c33cb300e11320fb11eb8d42b — the #334 change (resource.drop rejects dropping an owned resource while it is borrowed) together with the follow-up addressing the Codex review of that change (borrow registration at the canon-lower boundary with the transfer’s provenance, rejection of ownership transfers of borrowed entries, and borrow collection for every handle representation lowering accepts), merged with current main d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3 (PRs #350 and #351); ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45588402445, 45588419381 and 45588435815 against the branch and pull-request run 45588398739, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #352 (#334, resource.drop rejects dropping an owned resource while it is borrowed, plus the Codex-review follow-up on the same branch). The branch merged current main (merge commit 8ad5fb4, main at d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3 — PR #350 (#330) and PR #351 (#331) on top of the main at 4cdb5ae the branch had already merged for PR #348); the merge conflicted only in the vendored-suite exclusion table (the values/numerics.wast entry deleted by #330 in main and the resources/borrows.wast entry deleted by #334 here both stay deleted) and in the size-baseline files, which took main’s versions as the base for this re-baseline. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main alone (workflow_dispatch run 45588457205 on main at d5af7b8e004daff28d1735657155d3df5802d8a3; the run passes the gate against main’s checked-in baseline). Against the checked-in baseline, the main control is byte-identical on 29 of the 32 gated series; on the three release stripped-file series of the component-linking configurations it measures 32 B below that baseline, because that baseline was snapshotted from PR #350’s branch tree and the squash-merged main measures slightly smaller (the gate passes shrinkage, so the staleness was inert). This PR’s own delta against the main control is confined to the twelve series of the three configurations that link telomere-component: in release, stripped file +7,720 B (component), +7,704 B (wasi) and +7,720 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +7,584 B in each; in release-size, stripped file +5,464 B (component), +5,480 B (wasi) and +5,464 B (wasi-threads) and stripped .text +4,192 B, +4,208 B and +4,192 B. Every other configuration is byte-identical to main in both profiles. Those twelve series are re-baselined to the branch measurements; every other baseline is unchanged. Run-to-run spread was 0 B for every gated series across the four branch samples and the main control reproduced its tree exactly. Against the original #164 baseline, the largest cumulative growth is the release component stripped file series at +10.60% (2,433,656 B to 2,691,616 B); the release core-nosimd stripped file series is unchanged at +9.83% (1,275,448 B to 1,400,840 B). The core-aot configuration, added by PR #267 after the #164 baseline, is not part of the cumulative comparison.
